items.body:
### Related

  * PR for Chinese (Simplified) localization of the Rerun viewer UI

  ### What

  This PR adds a complete Chinese (Simplified) localization system to the Rerun viewer.

  **i18n framework**
  - New `Localizer` trait + `ChineseLocalizer` with **658 translation entries**
  - CJK font support: bundled NotoSansSC-VF as fallback for Chinese character rendering

  **Coverage (~80 files localized)**
  - Welcome screen, settings, top panel
  - Blueprint tree, viewport, context menu, selection panel
  - Time panel, recording panel, data UI, component UI
  - Spatial/dataframe/time-series/map/graph/text-log views
  - Memory panel, chunk store browser, server dialog, notifications
  - Tensor dimension mapper, pixel picking UI, and more

  **Technical details**
  - Uses a lightweight `t("key")` wrapper around a thread-safe global localizer
  - All translations stored in `crates/viewer/re_ui/src/zh_localizer.rs`
  - Built on v0.33.1, compiles with zero errors (`cargo build --release`)

  > Note: This PR was primarily developed through **vibecoding** — an AI-assisted approach where most of the code was
  generated and iterated on via natural language prompts with Claude (Anthropic's AI assistant). All changes were
  reviewed and compilation-verified.

items.title: When scrubbing time, intelligently round to a nice value
items.body:
### Related
* Part of https://linear.app/rerun/issue/RR-2768/improve-time-selection-experience-on-a-timeline

### What
When dragging the time cursor ("time scrubbing") we would previously pick arbitrarily precise time points, regardless of zoom level. Now, we snap to the "simplest" value that is within a pixel from the mouse cursor. The simplest value is defined as the one with _the most_ trailing zeroes (e.g. prefer `23.500000` over `23.484793`).

### Before
Even though we zoomed out to where we are viewing full hours, when we try to pick a time we select with microsecond precision:

![dumb-aim](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22a10523-a7a9-4474-909f-e61e11a8f551)


### After
Notice how we start by picking whole multiples of 10s, but as we zoom in we pick multiples of 0.5s, and then 5ms, 10us, etc.

![smart-aim](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9508f33-b724-43fe-8037-a4f5f33c0480)

Note that we only ever omit _zeroes_ in the display, so this is a real difference in how values are picked, NOT how they are displayed!


### Future work
* Coarser snapping when a modifier key is pressed
* Set the time display precision based on zoom level

items.title: Viewer now crops incoming chunks if time range was requested
items.body:
### Related

* Fixes https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/10692
* This is in many ways just part of a workaround for inspecting large episodes, making it related to https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/11315

### What

Datastore URLs allow querying only a time range. This then leads us to pulling down the necessary chunks, causing arbitrarily more data in the Viewer to arrive, depending on how big the chunks are.

This PR introduces crop-on-insert in order to crop chunks to the specified range, thus honoring the previously requested time bounds more accurately.
@abey79 and me decided to crop only on the specified timeline (not cropping on any other) and allow recombining cropped chunks into an existing store. This video demonstrates what this means in practice and feature some slight ui changes:


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/395223c3-4025-439f-a9ae-806f191713f2


While the cropping itself is a saimple range query on incoming chunks, in practice this gives rise to a whole slew of issues like how to deal with overlapping data, chunk ids, row ids, etc.. The most important ones like "what happens if I load the recording after all" & "what happens if I load overlapping ranges" are well-enough addressed here, but it's not a clean solution overall as you easily may end up in a situation with duplicated data in-memory.
I firmly believe that we should remove this mechanism again once we have dynamic occupancy handling for continuous streaming within a memory budget (#11315). We'll still want a way to highlight selected time ranges, but we can do that on a per-visualization basis as needed.

items.title: Support `BinaryStream` in `set_sinks()` for multi-sink streaming with Gradio

labels.name: 🪵 Log & send APIs
labels.description: Affects the user-facing API for all languages

items.body:
I HEAVILY used claude code for this, I did test with my gradio implementation to make sure it actually worked, and the changes are minimal so hopefully this is reasonable. 


### Related

<!--
Include links to any related issues/PRs in a bulleted list, for example:
* Closes #1234
* Part of #1337
-->
Closes rerun-io/rerun#11441

### What

<!--
Make sure the PR title and labels are set to maximize their usefulness for the CHANGELOG,
and our `git log`.

If you have noticed any breaking changes, include them in the migration guide.

We track various metrics at <https://build.rerun.io>.

For maintainers:
* To run all checks from `main`, comment on the PR with `@rerun-bot full-check`.
* To deploy documentation changes immediately after merging this PR, add the `deploy docs` label.

For more details check the PR section on <https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md>.
-->

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c03dd8f-146a-4c90-bd31-7294302a3d3a

Allow `BinaryStream` to be used alongside `FileSink` and `GrpcSink` in `set_sinks()`, enabling simultaneous streaming to a web viewer (Gradio in particular) and saving to disk from a single recording.

Previously, `set_sinks()` only accepted `FileSink` and `GrpcSink`, which meant Gradio apps that needed both live binary streaming and file persistence couldn't work. Now users can write:

    stream = recording.binary_stream()
    rr.set_sinks(rr.FileSink("output.rrd"), stream, recording=recording)

    recording.log(...)
    chunk = stream.read()   # for live viewer streaming
    # output.rrd also receives all logged data automatically

Implementation:
- Add `BinaryStreamStorage::create_sink()` to create a new `BinaryStreamSink` sharing the same `Arc<Mutex<...>>` buffer, so data written by the multi-sink can be read from the original storage.
- Implement `MultiSinkCompatible` (sealed trait) for `BinaryStreamSink` so it can participate in `MultiSink`.
- Add `PyBinarySinkStorage` downcast branch in the Python FFI `set_sinks()` to resolve `BinaryStream` objects into Rust sinks.
- Update Python `sinks.py` to include `BinaryStream` in `LogSinkLike` type alias and unwrap it to its inner storage before crossing the FFI boundary.

Minimal gradio example showing how to stream + save at the same time
```python
import time
import uuid
from collections.abc import Generator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Final

import cv2
import gradio as gr
import rerun as rr
import rerun.blueprint as rrb
from gradio_rerun import Rerun
from jaxtyping import UInt8
from numpy import ndarray

RRD_SAVE_DIR: Final[Path] = Path("data") / "rrd-gradio-saves"
RRD_SUFFIX: Final[str] = ".rrd"


def get_recording(recording_id: uuid.UUID | None, application_id: str = "Application ID") -> rr.RecordingStream:
    return rr.RecordingStream(application_id=application_id, recording_id=recording_id)


BLUR_BLUEPRINT = rrb.Blueprint(
    rrb.Horizontal(
        rrb.Spatial2DView(origin="image/original"),
        rrb.Spatial2DView(origin="image/blurred"),
    ),
    collapse_panels=True,
)


@dataclass(slots=True)
class SimpleAppState:
    """Session-local recording metadata and buffered stream bytes."""

    recording_id: uuid.UUID
    """Recording identifier reused for incremental logging."""
    rrd_buffer: bytearray = field(default_factory=bytearray)
    """In-memory copy of every chunk streamed to the viewer."""


def log_img_blur_multi_sink(
    state: SimpleAppState, image: UInt8[ndarray, "height width 3"]
) -> Generator[tuple[SimpleAppState, bytes], None, None]:
    recording: rr.RecordingStream = get_recording(recording_id=state.recording_id)

    # Create a binary stream bound to the recording
    stream: rr.BinaryStream = recording.binary_stream()

    # Use set_sinks to ALSO save to a file alongside the binary stream
    RRD_SAVE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    save_path = RRD_SAVE_DIR / f"{state.recording_id}{RRD_SUFFIX}"
    rr.set_sinks(
        rr.FileSink(str(save_path)),
        stream,
        recording=recording,
    )

    recording.send_blueprint(BLUR_BLUEPRINT)
    recording.set_time("iteration", sequence=0)
    recording.log("image/original", rr.Image(image))

    chunk: bytes | None = stream.read()
    if chunk is not None:
        yield state, chunk

    blur: UInt8[ndarray, "height width 3"] = image.copy()
    for i in range(50):
        recording.set_time("iteration", sequence=i)

        time.sleep(0.1)
        blur = cv2.GaussianBlur(blur, (5, 5), 0)
        recording.log("image/blurred", rr.Image(blur))

        chunk = stream.read()
        if chunk is not None:
            yield state, chunk

    chunk = stream.read()
    if chunk is not None:
        yield state, chunk


def verify_and_return_rrd(state: SimpleAppState) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    """Return the saved .rrd file for download and verify its contents."""
    save_path = RRD_SAVE_DIR / f"{state.recording_id}{RRD_SUFFIX}"
    if not save_path.exists():
        return None, "No saved .rrd file found."

    file_path = str(save_path)

    try:
        recording = rr.recording.load_recording(save_path)
        schema = recording.schema()

        entity_paths = schema.entity_paths()
        archetypes = schema.archetypes()
        index_names = [c.name for c in schema.index_columns()]

        has_original = any("image/original" in p for p in entity_paths)
        has_blurred = any("image/blurred" in p for p in entity_paths)
        has_iteration = "iteration" in index_names

        lines = [
            f"Verified {save_path.name}:",
            f"  Entity paths: {entity_paths}",
            f"  Archetypes: {archetypes}",
            f"  Timelines: {index_names}",
            f"  image/original present: {has_original}",
            f"  image/blurred present: {has_blurred}",
            f"  'iteration' timeline: {has_iteration}",
            f"  File size: {save_path.stat().st_size / 1024:.1f} KB",
        ]

        if not has_original or not has_blurred:
            lines.append("  WARNING: Missing expected entity paths!")
        if not has_iteration:
            lines.append("  WARNING: Missing 'iteration' timeline!")

        return file_path, "\n".join(lines)
    except Exception as e:
        return file_path, f"Verification failed: {e}"


def build() -> gr.Blocks:
    with gr.Blocks() as demo:
        session_state: gr.State = gr.State(SimpleAppState(recording_id=uuid.uuid4()))

        with gr.Row():
            with gr.Column(scale=2):
                input_image: gr.Image = gr.Image(
                    label="Input Image",
                    type="numpy",
                    image_mode="RGB",
                )
                gr.Examples(
                    examples=[
                        ["https://huggingface.co/datasets/pablovela5620/minicoco/resolve/main/000000000785.jpg"],
                        ["https://huggingface.co/datasets/pablovela5620/minicoco/resolve/main/000000001296.jpg"],
                    ],
                    inputs=[input_image],
                    cache_examples=False,
                )
                blur_button: gr.Button = gr.Button("Blur Image (Multi-Sink)")
                download_file: gr.File = gr.File(label="Saved .rrd File")
                verify_output: gr.Textbox = gr.Textbox(label="Verification Result", lines=5)
            with gr.Column(scale=5):
                rerun_viewer: Rerun = Rerun(
                    streaming=True,
                    panel_states={
                        "time": "collapsed",
                        "blueprint": "collapsed",
                        "selection": "collapsed",
                    },
                )

        blur_button.click(
            log_img_blur_multi_sink,
            inputs=[session_state, input_image],
            outputs=[session_state, rerun_viewer],
        ).then(
            verify_and_return_rrd,
            inputs=[session_state],
            outputs=[download_file, verify_output],
        )

    return demo


if __name__ == "__main__":
    build().launch()
```

items.body:
### Related

* Closes #7728

### What

Makes time cursor and current timeline be controlled by the blueprint.

### Details

We log the time as static for blueprints for it not to affect undo state.

This includes some refactors that felt necessary to make tests still work and not be overly complicated:
- `TestContext` doesn't require a mutable reference to run.
- Can update `TestContext` blueprints via `TestContext::with_blueprint_ctx`.
- The blueprint ctx is a struct that implements a helper trait for interacting with blueprints. App also has an equivalent `AppBlueprintCtx`, and `ViewerContext` also implements this trait.
- `TimeControl` is no longer stored behind an `RwLock` in app, and instead interacted with through sending `SystemCommand::TimeControlCommands`.

The time panel was refactored a bit to allow the normal time panel and blueprint inspector time panel to still share code. This is mostly changing `&mut TimeControl` to `&mut impl TimeControlCtx` which handles writing to blueprints/just updating time control whether this is the blueprint inspector time panel or not.

items.title: Add selection change and time(line) change callbacks to Jupyter Notebook and JS APIs

labels.name: 🕸️ web
labels.description: regarding running the viewer in a browser

items.body:
* Part of https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/9169

## What

This PR adds basic selection and timeline callbacks to the Viewer:
* `selectionchange`: Fired when an item is selected.
  * We only expose `View`, `Container`, `Entity`, and `Instance`.
* `timelinechange`: Fired when the active timeline changes.
* `timeupdate`: Fired when the time on the active timeline changes.

These callbacks are exposed in the Web Viewer:

```ts
// We use the Node `EventEmitter` pattern in JS:
viewer.on("selectionchange", (selection) => console.log(selection));
```

And in Jupyter Notebooks:

```py
from rerun_notebook import Viewer, ViewerCallbacks

# We (Jan and Gijs) chose to expose this as a class that you inherit from:
class MyCallbacks(ViewerCallbacks):
  def on_selection_change(self, selection):
    print(selection)

# Which is then passed to a `Viewer` instance:
viewer = Viewer()
viewer.register_callbacks(MyCallbacks())
```

Because of how these callbacks pass through the Web Viewer, they are technically also exposed in Rust, via `StartupOptions`. I'm not sure how far we want to take that, so I didn't expose it all the way through the top-level `rerun` crate.
